source: Gómez-Boix et al. 2018 (Hiding in the Crowd)
_meta.license: Figures quoted from the cited papers with attribution. Gómez-Boix et al. 2018 and Berke et al. 2025 are CC BY 4.0; Andriamilanto et al. 2022 (ACM/arXiv) and Eckersley 2010 (Springer) are cited as individual facts. No dataset-derived numbers.
_meta.notes: Shannon bits per attribute from fingerprinting studies (population averages, not the visitor's value); leftover = bits left given the most informative other attribute. Bits from different attributes must not be added and never divide a crowd count. Full method notes: SOURCES.md. Compilation CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (LICENSE); each source keeps its own licence.

gomezboix2018.cite: Gómez-Boix et al. 2018 (Hiding in the Crowd)
gomezboix2018.citation: Alejandro Gómez-Boix, Pierre Laperdrix, Benoit Baudry. 2018. Hiding in the Crowd: an Analysis of the Effectiveness of Browser Fingerprinting at Large Scale. In Proceedings of The Web Conference 2018 (WWW 2018), Lyon, France, 309–318.
gomezboix2018.license: CC BY 4.0 (stated in the paper: 'published under Creative Commons CC BY 4.0 License')
gomezboix2018.table: Table 3 (Shannon entropy, bits and normalized, for all devices, mobile devices and desktop/laptop machines)
gomezboix2018.population: Visitors of two pages (weather forecast, political news) of one top-15 French website who accepted cookies
gomezboix2018.caveat: French audience: time zone and language entropy are near zero. 17 correlated attributes; their per-attribute bits sum to 53.7 against a 20.98-bit maximum. Data predates Chrome's User-Agent reduction, hard-coded plugin lists and Safari/Firefox/Brave canvas, WebGL and audio noise.

andriamilanto2022.citation: Nampoina Andriamilanto, Tristan Allard, Gaëtan Le Guelvouit, Alexandre Garel. 2022. A Large-scale Empirical Analysis of Browser Fingerprints Properties for Web Authentication. ACM Transactions on the Web 16(1), Article 4, 4:1–4:62 (published online October 2021).
andriamilanto2022.license: arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (not CC); individual figures cited as facts with attribution
andriamilanto2022.table: Appendix E, Table 16 (distinct values, normalized entropy, MinNCE, stability) and Table 5 (minimum conditional entropy in bits for MinNCE > 0.045)
andriamilanto2022.population: Visitors of the same French top-15 website and experiment as Gómez-Boix et al. 2018 (news and weather pages)

uniqueShareTimePartitioned.note: Unicity rate of the time-partitioned datasets as printed in the paper ('81.3%'; mobile vs desktop 'approximately 42% against 84%'). uniqueShare.all 0.818 is the complete dataset.

andriamilanto2022.caveat: Per-attribute values cover all devices only (no desktop/mobile split). MinNCE is conditional on the single most informative other attribute, which may not be a step of our funnel, so the leftover is a rough floor. Same French bias and age as Gómez-Boix et al. 2018.

berke2025.citation: Alex Berke, Enrico Bacis, Badih Ghazi, Pritish Kamath, Ravi Kumar, Robin Lassonde, Pasin Manurangsi, Umar Syed. 2025. How Unique is Whose Web Browser? The Role of Demographics in Browser Fingerprinting among US Users. Proceedings on Privacy Enhancing Technologies 2025(1), 720–758.
berke2025.license: CC BY 4.0 (paper). The underlying dataset's terms forbid re-publication; only figures printed in the paper are used.
berke2025.table: Table 1 (distinct values, % unique, Shannon entropy in bits) and Table 6 (distinct and % unique for the full attribute set)
berke2025.population: 8,400 consenting US adults recruited on Prolific (attributes collected with FingerprintJS-style JavaScript); Windows over-represented (50.2% vs 35.3% StatCounter US)
berke2025.caveat: Small sample: entropy is capped at log2(8400) = 13.04 bits, so high-cardinality attributes are understated. US only. No desktop/mobile split. No entropy is reported for canvas, fonts or audio.

eckersley2010.citation: Peter Eckersley. 2010. How Unique Is Your Web Browser? In Privacy Enhancing Technologies (PETS 2010), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, Springer, 1–18.
eckersley2010.license: © Springer; EFF hosts an authorized copy. Individual figures cited as facts with attribution.
eckersley2010.table: Appendix, Table 2 (mean surprisal for each variable in isolation, bits)
eckersley2010.population: Self-selected, privacy-interested visitors of panopticlick.eff.org, worldwide
eckersley2010.caveat: Plugin and font lists came from Flash/Java and NPAPI plugins, which no longer exist. No canvas, WebGL or audio. Audience bias.

canvas.label: Canvas image
canvas.note: Canvas bits depend strongly on the drawing test: three canvases in one study scored 7.76–9.23 bits. Ours is 'similar to', not 'the same as', these tests. Safari, Firefox (fingerprinting protection) and Brave add noise, so the value may be randomized. Berke et al. 2025 report no entropy for canvas (Table 6: 951 distinct text-canvas values, 7.9% unique among 8,400).

facts.text: Per-attribute bits cannot be added: Panopticlick's eight attributes sum to 55.7 bits, but the whole fingerprint carried at least 18.1 bits.
Hiding in the Crowd's 17 attributes sum to 53.7 bits against a 20.98-bit maximum, and only 33.6% of fingerprints were unique (35.7% desktop, 18.5% mobile).
facts.cite: Gómez-Boix et al. 2018 (Hiding in the Crowd), Table 3 (PDF p. 7); abstract

facts.text: In a 2023 US sample of 8,400 browsers, 13 attributes combined gave 12.1 bits (of 13.04 possible) and 60.2% unique fingerprints.
The WebGL renderer carried 6.83 bits when unmasked but 0.78 bits in its masked form; 'Apple GPU' was the most common unmasked value.
